## Background

![](https://subelab.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/2016-PNAS-Krumhansla.jpg){fig-align="center"}

## Background
- In 2013, we collected all extant time series of kelp abundance
- Analysis showed 1/3 of the world's forests declining, 1/3 with no trend, 1/3 increasing
- We decided to revisit a decade later
- BUT - starting with Northwest Atlantic to build framework so that we can move on to the rest of the world more quickly

## Variation in Measurement type
Standardized as $stdkelp = Kelp_{ijt}/m_{ij}$
m = average of highest three measurement  
i = ecoregion (or whole data set)
j = measurement type  
t = year
```{r measure_type}

traj_dat <- nwa_dat |>
  select(ecoregion,
         trajectory,
         has_bm, 
         has_sd,
         has_pc) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(ecoregion, trajectory)) |>
  filter(value>0) |>
  group_by(ecoregion, name) |>
  summarize(n_timeseries = n_distinct(trajectory)) |>
  mutate(name = case_when(
    name == "has_bm" ~ "Biomass",
    name == "has_sd" ~ "Stipe density",
    name == "has_pc" ~ "Percent cover"
  ))

ggplot(traj_dat |> filter(!is.na(ecoregion)),
       aes(y = ecoregion, x = name, 
           fill = n_timeseries,
           label = n_timeseries)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_label(fontface="bold") +
  labs(x = "", y = "") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top", 
                   expand = c(0,0))  +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu",
                       trans = "log10", 
                       guide = "none") +
  theme_classic()
```

## A function to get predictions and spatial variation
```{r get_predicted_sdm_data}
#| echo: true
get_predicted_sdm_data <-
  function(mod, dat = NULL, 
           nsim = 300, slopevar = "year_c",
           lwr = 0.025, upr = 0.975){
  if(is.null(dat)){
    dat <- mod$data
    dat$yi <- mod$tmb_data$y_i
  }
  
  # for combined variable    
  # from the paper
  zeta_s <- predict(mod, newdata = dat,
                    nsim = nsim, 
                    sims_var = "zeta_s")
  
  sims <- spread_sims(mod, nsim = nsim)
  
  combined <- sims[[slopevar]] + t(zeta_s)
  dat$combined_slope_median <- apply(combined, 2, median)
  dat$combined_slope_mean <- apply(combined, 2, mean)
  dat$combined_slope_sd <- apply(combined, 2, sd)
  dat$combined_slope_lwr <- apply(combined, 2, quantile, 
                                  probs = 0.025)
  dat$combined_slope_upr <- apply(combined, 2, quantile, 
                                  probs = 0.975)
  
  predict(mod, se=TRUE, newdata = dat) |>
    mutate(slope_fe = coef(mod)[2],
           slope_fe_se = tidy(mod)$std.error[2])
}
```

## Spatio-Temporal Variation

- We know that there has been urchin outbreaks, recovery, species invasions, climate change, and more in the region  

- GAMs seem the right way to go to examine temporal variation 

- But, the severity and timing of these mechanisms differ by region. 

## A Function to Generate Elements Needed for GAMs in sdmTMB

```{r make_basis_function}
#| echo: true
make_basis <- function(smooth_formula, dat, basis_prev = NULL){
  sm <- sdmTMB:::parse_smoothers(smooth_formula, data = dat, basis_prev = basis_prev)
  
  # unpenalized v. penalized part
  sx <- as.data.frame(sm$Xs)
  colnames(sx) <- paste0("SX", seq_len(ncol(sx)))
  sz <- as.data.frame(do.call(cbind, sm$Zs))
  colnames(sz) <- paste0("SZ", seq_len(ncol(sz)))
  
  # or the whole thing
  v <- as_tibble(sm$basis_out[[1]][[1]]$X)
  
  # data with basis sets
  dat <- cbind(dat, sx, sz, v)
  
  return(list(sx = sx, sz = sz, dat = dat, sm = sm, v = v))
}
```

## Creating a smoother and basis set

```{r make_basis}
#| echo: true
# the smoother - k = 5 as ~5 decades
smooth_formula <- 
  focal_std_by_all ~ s(year,  bs = "tp", k = 5)


nwa_basis <- make_basis(smooth_formula, nwa_dat)
nwa_dat_with_basis <- nwa_basis$dat
```

## Making Unpenalized Formulae

```{r gam_formulae}
#| echo: true
fe_formula_unpenalized <- 
  as.formula(paste("focal_std_by_all ~ 1 + ",
                   paste(colnames(nwa_basis$v), collapse = " + "),
                   "+ (1|study) + (1  |trajectory)"))

svc_formula_unpenalized <- 
  as.formula(paste("~ 0 +",
                   paste(colnames(nwa_basis$v), collapse = " + ")))
```

## Making Unpenalized Formulae

```{r show_formulae}
#| echo: true

fe_formula_unpenalized

svc_formula_unpenalized

```

## Putting This Into sdmTMB
```{r mod_spatiotemporal}
#| echo: true
mod_spatiotemporal<- sdmTMB(
  fe_formula_unpenalized,
  spatial_varying = svc_formula_unpenalized, 
  
  dispformula = ~focalUnit,
  family = tweedie(link = "log"),
  
  spatial = "on",
  mesh = mesh_coastline,
  
  data = nwa_dat_with_basis,
  control = 
    sdmTMBcontrol(map = list(ln_tau_Z = factor(rep(1L, ncol(nwa_basis$v)))))
)
```

## Rate of Change

```{r derivs}
#| echo: true
get_derivs <- function(dat){
  dat |>
    group_by(X, Y, ecoregion, trajectory, study, geometry) |>
    arrange(year) |>
    mutate(est_change = lead(est) - lag(est),
           log_est_change = log(lead(est)+1e-7) - log(lag(est)+1e-7),
           est_accel = lead(est_change) - lag(est_change) ) |>
    ungroup()
}
```

## Final Thoughts on GAM sdmTMB
- We see surprising uniformity in loss and recovery

- Are things tuned right?

- A little worried that S trend is not stronger, but, this is because here we have a spatial RE instead of a spatial FE (conversation point) 

- Is implementation of GAM here correct?
